goals: Estimate basin runoff generation (QOVER + QDRAI) across the Naches/American River elevation-precip gradient
Validation: reproduce the daily streamflow hydrograph at the American River gauge and report NSE (as-posed target)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves the vertical water balance and snow physics that generate runoff; NLDAS-2 resolves the orographic gradient across 1625 m of relief.

answerable: Per-column runoff-generation fluxes (QOVER, QDRAI, QRUNOFF) and snow/SWE across the elevation-precip gradient
Unrouted, area-weighted basin runoff VOLUME at monthly/annual scale (approximate water balance)

not_answerable.aspect: Daily streamflow hydrograph at the gauge and its NSE
not_answerable.why: Single-column, no lateral transport, no routing, no native integrated streamflow — grid runoff cannot be converted to a gauge discharge time series, and daily NSE is dominated by routing/timing the stack cannot represent
not_answerable.needs: runoff aggregation + channel routing over the contributing area

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified along the elevation/forcing gradient with native soil
sampling_strategy.n_justification: Three elevation/precip bands (NLDAS resolves ~15 precip values over this relief) x ~3 columns per band to span the rain-snow transition and native soil variability; the smallest set that spans the runoff-generation gradient of the contributing area.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate at the rain-snow transition (largest melt-timing sensitivity) and along the upper-basin contributing area draining to the American River gauge; anchor one low-elevation column near the gauge.
sampling_strategy.replication: Light (~3 per band) to capture soil/aspect spread within a band; no dense replication given no routing to exploit it.

sampling_plan.reason: Captures low-elevation rain-driven runoff and the near-gauge water balance.
Highest melt-timing sensitivity; controls the seasonal runoff pulse shape.
Dominant SWE storage and spring melt source for the contributing area.

validation_design.observation_source: USGS gauge: American River nr Nile (daily)
validation_design.comparison: aggregated — would require summing area-weighted column QRUNOFF and routing to the gauge; NOT possible in current stack, so daily NSE cannot be computed. Only unrouted monthly/annual runoff VOLUME can be compared as a coarse check.
validation_design.metric: NSE (requested, but BLOCKED); monthly runoff-volume bias as the only currently-supportable proxy

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.capability: runoff aggregation + channel routing over the contributing area
requires_capabilities.why: Convert independent-column QRUNOFF into a gauge discharge time series with correct timing
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire as-posed target: daily hydrograph and NSE

requires_capabilities.why: Define which columns and areas drain to the American River gauge for weighting
Ingest observed hydrograph and score against a routed simulation
Baseflow/drainage (QDRAI) requires realistic initial water table

assumptions: Basin lies within CONUS so NLDAS-2 12 km forcing (elevation-resolved) applies.
Snow/SWE default output is sufficient for the snowmelt runoff signal.
Multi-year spin-up (or WTD warm start) is included so drainage/baseflow are not initialization artifacts.
open_questions: Is any routing/aggregation post-processor acceptable, or must NSE be from a fully coupled routed run?
What is the gauge's contributing drainage area, to bound the columns and area weights?
Is a monthly runoff-volume comparison an acceptable interim deliverable given daily NSE is not currently computable?
